UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile information, used to associate meetings with a specific user. Authentication details are handled externally.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. This typically comes from an external authentication system.

email.description: The email address associated with the user profile.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was last updated.

Meeting.title: Meeting
Meeting.description: Represents a single business meeting with its details, scheduled by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Meeting entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who owns or scheduled this meeting. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Meeting)

title.description: The descriptive title or subject of the meeting.

startDateTime.description: The exact date and time when the meeting is scheduled to begin, in ISO 8601 format.

endDateTime.description: The exact date and time when the meeting is scheduled to end, in ISO 8601 format.

location.description: The physical or virtual location where the meeting will take place.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the meeting record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the meeting record was last updated.

definition.description: Stores individual user profile information. The document ID for each user profile will be the Firebase Authentication UID. Access is restricted to the owner.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user.

definition.description: Stores individual meeting details for a specific user. This is a subcollection under the user's profile. Each document includes a denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user who owns the meeting.

params.name: meetingId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific meeting.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore structure prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the core design principles. User profiles are stored in a top-level collection `/users`, with each document's ID being the user's authenticated UID. User-specific meetings are stored in a subcollection under their respective user profile: `/users/{userId}/meetings`. This hierarchical, path-based ownership is highly secure and straightforward to manage.

**Authorization Independence:**
To achieve Authorization Independence (CRITICAL principle), every `Meeting` document stored under `/users/{userId}/meetings/{meetingId}` will include a `userId` field that explicitly identifies its owner. This `userId` field must match the `{userId}` wildcard in the path, which in turn must match `request.auth.uid`. This denormalization means that Firestore Security Rules can determine authorization solely by inspecting the `resource.data.userId` field within the `Meeting` document itself, and comparing it to `request.auth.uid` and the path parameter `{userId}`. This eliminates the need for expensive and complex `get()` calls to parent documents in security rules, allowing for atomic writes and reads, and simplifying rule logic. For example, a user can create a meeting without the rules needing to read their `UserProfile` document first to confirm ownership.

**QAPs (Secure List Operations):**
The structural segregation directly supports Query Authorization Patterns (QAPs). By placing meetings in `/users/{userId}/meetings`, `list` operations become inherently secure. A client requesting a list of meetings would query `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid).collection('meetings')`. Firestore Security Rules for this path can simply check `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. Because `userId` is a path parameter derived directly from `request.auth.uid`, the query *itself* limits the scope to only the authenticated user's data. This ensures that Firestore does not have to act as a filter, and only authorized data is ever returned, fulfilling the QAP mandate.
